title: Compose the model-driven surface deterministically before any call
statement: A screen whose layout is produced by a model shows nothing but a 'go talk to the assistant' prompt to every user who never opens the chat, so a large widget registry earns nothing. Build the same spec shape deterministically from state already reachable client-side, label it as the fallback, let the model's spec always take precedence when present, and keep the composer pure so it stays unit-testable.

title: Write a rejected agent action back into the transcript
statement: Silently discarding an action the dispatcher refused produces the worst outcome: the model's prose already told the user it happened, and next turn it re-emits the same action. Append a system message naming the action, the reason and what to do instead — surface it, pivot, or acknowledge the gap — so consequences are in context by construction rather than by a bespoke re-prompt.

title: Serialize the form's answers into the intent so the model won't re-ask
statement: When a UI collects structured choices and then hands an intent to a model that interrogates the user for the same things, the user answers everything twice. Append a deterministic, human-readable summary of those choices to the prompt so the model's clarifying-question heuristics read them as already answered — including explicit negatives, because an omitted choice reads as unset rather than declined.

title: Make a metered AI route a spec object, not hand-rolled pipeline code
statement: Every charged AI route repeats the same sequence — parse, rate-limit, charge, call, guard, persist, respond — and every hand-rolled copy gets one of the ordering invariants wrong. Own the pipeline once and let a route declare only its own parse, prompt, guard and persist hooks, so rules like 'rate-limit before charge' and 'a reclaimed charge is never billed' hold by construction.

title: Collapse a policy vocabulary onto a narrower toggle by failing safe
statement: Mapping a rich authored vocabulary onto a narrower runtime enum always leaves a catch-all branch, and putting the permissive value there quietly turns unknown or nuanced policies into 'skip the guard'. Enumerate only the values that legitimately mean skip, send everything else including unknown values to the guarded side, and lock the mapping with a named regression test.

title: Resume by real session handle, degrade to a reconstructed hint
statement: Continuing a cancelled or failed model-driven run should first try true provider-side session resumption; only when no session handle survives should it fall back to a fresh call carrying a hint rebuilt from what was actually observed. Model the two paths as a tagged union rather than an optional string so the degraded case is explicit at the type level, and write the summary that hint needs at cancel time.

title: Funnel every model call through one provider-agnostic function
statement: Feature code that imports a provider SDK directly spreads model configuration, caching and failure handling across every route. Route all generation through a single provider-agnostic function that resolves the provider from the environment, applies the response cache, and returns a null-shaped result callers treat as 'use the deterministic fallback' rather than an exception to catch ad hoc.

title: Ban provider SDK imports outside the call seam with a lint rule
statement: A documented 'always call through our wrapper' rule is invisible to the fortieth route someone adds later. Make the boundary physical: a restricted-import rule that rejects the provider SDK everywhere except the seam directory, so a bypass fails lint instead of relying on review. The seam itself stays a dispatcher over interchangeable engines.

title: Keep providers dumb; put cross-cutting AI concerns in the dispatcher
statement: If each provider implements its own cost ceiling, empty-response detection, quality gating and logging, the engines drift and every caller must know which one it got. Let a provider do only the raw call and its error mapping, and give the dispatcher every shared post-processing step, so all engines behave identically at the call site.

title: Apply guardrails and telemetry as decorators built once at the seam
statement: Cross-cutting behaviour written inside each engine drifts, and the drift is silent — one engine stops reporting errors and nobody notices for months. Expose one minimal generate interface, layer guardrails and cost/latency telemetry as decorators applied once at construction, and state what each layer deliberately does not do so it cannot creep into responsibilities that belong per-route.

title: Load providers lazily and order the seam decorators deliberately
statement: Importing every provider SDK at the seam drags all of them into the bundle and couples the app to engines it will never select. Import the chosen provider lazily, and treat decorator order as load-bearing: tracing outermost so cache hits still emit a trace, cache innermost so identical retries skip the round-trip, with trace flushes scheduled off the request path so a billed call never waits on telemetry.

title: Refuse silent cross-provider fallback on a money-critical path
statement: Silently switching engines when the configured one fails hides a misconfiguration exactly where it costs most. When a provider is explicitly forced, return that engine or nothing and never the alternate, so the failure surfaces loudly; apply shared concerns such as response caching as a wrapper around whichever engine was chosen so the decision does not change behaviour elsewhere.

title: Separate the fallback ordering policy from provider execution
statement: Fallback logic entangled with SDK loading can only be tested with network mocks, so in practice it is not tested at all. Express candidate ordering as a pure function of engine availability plus preference, with development-only engines last, keep invocation and telemetry outside it, and terminate the list in a deterministic template so a keyless build still produces something.

title: Make failover an explicit ordering policy with telemetry on every hop
statement: Refusing all failover and cascading silently are both wrong: one trades availability, the other hides misconfiguration on the path that costs money. Express failover as a pure, testable candidate-ordering function separated from execution and record every hop in telemetry — and treat a fallback chain that covers a secondary capability but not the primary one as an inconsistency rather than a design.

title: Route model and effort per turn class from one calibrated table
statement: One model and effort setting for the whole product either overpays on trivial calls or underperforms on the hard ones. Classify calls by what they must be good at and put each class's choice in a single table beside the measurement that justified it. Two findings are worth carrying: lowering effort can be free, and adding doctrine to a low-effort micro call can regress it.

title: Bind a provider per pipeline stage behind one chat trait
statement: Different stages of a pipeline have different quality needs, so one global model choice either overpays everywhere or underperforms where it matters. Define one narrow chat trait, implement it once per provider family (a single OpenAI-compatible implementation covers many by base-URL swap), and let a router hold a provider per named stage so model choice becomes central configuration rather than call-site code.

title: Keep provider selection pure and gate per-request overrides
statement: Provider choice that lives inside the SDK-loading code cannot be unit tested without loading an SDK or spawning a subprocess. Resolve it in a pure string-parsing module, and if a per-request header may override the environment choice, put that behind an explicit off-by-default flag — otherwise a client can force a production deploy into an engine that was only ever meant for local development.

title: Wire the resilience stack to your main surface, not a side capability
statement: A provider abstraction carrying cache, rate limiting, circuit breaking and cost tracking earns nothing if the app's primary generation surface routes around it. When fallback chains exist for secondary capabilities while the main one is empty and marked deprecated, that is an unfinished migration rather than a design decision — name it as such and finish it.

title: Treat a spawned CLI as a dev or agentic engine, never the prod path
statement: Shelling out to a locally installed model CLI is legitimate for local development and for genuinely agentic, tool-using work, but it makes every deploy depend on a developer-machine binary. Put an API provider behind the same interface as the production default and keep the CLI an opt-in engine chosen by the same selector, so the two are interchangeable rather than parallel systems.

title: Cap every generated context block with its own budget, reserve footer space, and make truncated lists say N of M
statement: A bounded block appends rows only while they fit after reserving space for an honesty footer, so the footer can never be squeezed out — a truncated list that does not say it is truncated makes the consumer conclude the missing item does not exist. Budgets are deliberately not shared between features (adding one digest cannot silently shrink another), and a compile-time assert pins the sum.

title: Log per-block size AND a stable content hash of assembled prompts — and prove the instrumentation is byte-neutral
statement: A block can hold its char count exactly and still be rewritten every turn, which is what invalidates a prompt cache; sizes answer how big, only a hash answers did it change. Use a hash stable across toolchain upgrades (FNV-1a-64, not DefaultHasher), and pin the composed output byte-for-byte with a test so measurement can never perturb the thing measured.

title: Back an LLM-powered generator with a deterministic fallback in the same call site
statement: A UX flow that asks an LLM to generate a structured artifact (team topology from a description) should catch the LLM path's failure and fall through to the deterministic heuristic version of the same command — the user gets a usable draft either way, and the empty-result case ('no agents matched') is handled as its own explicit outcome rather than as an error.

title: Measure regression against a pinned baseline on the same axis
statement: Non-deterministic output has no absolute pass mark, so quality regression has to be a delta. Pin a baseline variant explicitly rather than comparing against whatever ran last, compute the delta only when the same-model, same-scenario pair actually exists — cross-axis deltas are noise, so the honest value is null — and flag drops past a named threshold constant.

title: Write output quality gates as pure functions shared by CI and replay
statement: A gate that exists only inside a test cannot check production output, and a runtime check cannot tell you that a prompt edit made things worse. Define pass/warn/fail gates as I/O-free functions over prompt construction, fallback templates and live output, then run the identical functions from CI, from a local verbose runner, and over replayed production traces.

title: Pin every model surface with offline gates, not runtime checks alone
statement: Runtime grounding checks catch a bad answer in the moment but cannot tell you that a prompt or model change made the surface worse overall. Ship pure gate or golden-fixture functions that run identically in CI, in replay and against live output, so a regression is caught by the same assertions wherever it shows up.

title: Feed the judge's rationale into the rewriter, not just its scores
statement: An eval harness produces both numbers and free-text diagnosis, and piping four averaged scalars into 'now improve this prompt' throws away the only part that says why it failed. Ground the improvement call server-side in the full current prompt plus the per-scenario rationale and suggestions, and persist the result as a new versioned variant rather than a chat suggestion.

title: Show a judge's verdict only beside hard gates and what was delivered
statement: A model-produced quality score is one input, not a certification. Render it next to objective pass/fail gates with their log tails, the commit and file list of what was actually delivered, and a per-source grounding table — so a confident verdict over an empty or unsourced deliverable is visibly different from a real one.

title: Compute the composite score in one module and re-export it everywhere
statement: When grids, reports, cards and detail panels each rank variants by a weighted composite, any inline re-derivation produces surfaces that disagree about which variant won. Keep the weights and the rounding in exactly one module, re-export it from the feature barrel so consumers cannot reach past it, and pin the formula with a golden test.

title: Treat an unscored judge metric as absent, never as zero
statement: Judges time out, fail, or decline a dimension. Coercing that null to zero drags every average down and makes a broken run look like a bad model. Accumulate a scored-count per metric rather than one count per row, divide by it, and render an em dash wherever a metric was never scored so 'not measured' stays visibly different from 'measured badly'.

title: Ship each score with its provenance: samples, coverage, degraded runs
statement: A judged score is only as trustworthy as the run that produced it. Persist the sample count, whether all sub-scores were covered, and how many samples fell back to a heuristic when the judge failed, then surface that inline with a warning affordance and carry the same provenance into any exported report — so a degraded number is never read as equivalent to a clean one.

title: Parse agent protocol lines tolerantly, but the JSON span strictly
statement: Find the protocol marker anywhere in the line, slice the {..} span, then deserialize strictly. A strict `strip_prefix` lost 7 of 8 verdicts to a leading "- VERDICT:" the model added.

title: Index agent verdicts by POSITION, never by an echoed identifier
statement: Model-echoed UUIDs mismark the wrong practice; index verdicts by position instead. Out-of-range verdicts are dropped with a visible [Ignored]; repeats are first-wins.

title: Reconcile 'asked' vs 'landed' and name the gap
statement: After a fan-out, compute selected/checked/lost and emit a warning naming the gap; count capped-away proposals as dropped rather than losing them silently.

title: Size an LLM batch from a MEASURED failure and write the measurement into the constant
statement: Batch sizes come from observed failure, not guesswork: 25 practices produced 0 verdicts in a 15-min window; 8 = ~2min/practice + margin. The measurement is written into the constant's comment so the number stays justified.

title: Instruct STREAMING emission — batched-at-end output is lost on timeout
statement: Prompt the agent to emit results as it goes; batched-at-end output is entirely lost when the run times out ("a 25-practice run did exactly that and returned nothing").

title: Content-hash the tree and feed the LLM only the delta
statement: Hash file contents so incremental scans feed the LLM only changed files; `cache_empty` explicitly signals full-scan-required; the walk runs in spawn_blocking with a skip-list, symlink skip, and 2MB per-file cap.

title: Feed a scan its own rejections so it cannot REPHRASE a durable no
statement: Include existing plus archived/rejected names in prompts and rejected_dedup_keys in the snapshot — the digest exists because DB dedup blocks exact re-emission but not rewording.

title: Extract stream phase purely, returning null whenever visible text is the signal
statement: A pure stream-phase extractor returns null when text is arriving (the visible text IS the progress signal) and for system events (empirically mapped to a stuck "Connecting…"), with per-tool curated detail extraction clipped to 40-48 chars — never raw telemetry — and unknown tools falling through to a template.

title: Regenerate injected prompt sections idempotently: strip by marker, then merge under user-owned keys
statement: Machine-generated sections inside a user-editable document (prompt, instructions) need (a) a stable marker so regeneration strips the prior copy up to the next section boundary before appending, and (b) merge semantics where existing/user-authored keys always win over freshly-derived ones — so re-derivation is idempotent and never clobbers tuning.

title: Fan-in pipeline nodes need a deterministic all-predecessors context digest
statement: When each pipeline node runs in a fresh process/context, passing only the latest predecessor's raw output silently drops every other upstream branch at fan-in points — build a deterministic (no extra model call) digest of ALL completed predecessors at a configurable fidelity and attach it alongside the primary input.

title: Checkpoint each agent-run stage as a git commit on a per-run branch
statement: Agents mutating a real repository should commit every completed stage onto a dedicated per-run branch (with trailers carrying run id + stage), giving a run that goes sideways a clean rewind point and a fork-from-here recovery using plain git — with auto-maintenance and signing disabled so checkpoints stay fast and deterministic.

title: Cap an LLM survey by territory, not by item count
statement: A 'return at most N high-signal items' brief over a large corpus is satisfiable without doing the survey — the agent mines the cheapest ground, hits the cap, and stops. Bound the work by assigning each session ONE named territory (with its file paths and last-visited date) and remove the item cap entirely; volume is then bounded by what the territory genuinely contains, and machine guards (max items per ingest, max payload bytes) catch runaways.

title: Centralize agent-dispatch consent into one surface with a pre-flight prepare() that aborts on failure
statement: When several transports can hand work to an agent, route them all through one consent surface (editable prompt, radiogroup semantics, dedup against already-running sessions) that accepts a `prepare()` hook running AFTER user confirm but BEFORE the transport — throwing aborts the dispatch, so a half-prepared target never gets a session pointed at it. Document deliberate asymmetries (no dedup for transports the app holds no handle on).

title: Refuse to re-run agent work without the original task context
statement: An automated continuation/retry of agent work must abort when the original input is missing or unparseable, rather than starting a contextless re-run. NULL and unparseable inputs silently collapsing to None produce a run that fabricates work off a hallucinated reconstruction — potentially taking real, irreversible actions — while logging a 'successful continuation'. Abort, leave the item claimed-but-not-continued, and surface it for a human.

title: Payloads destined for an LLM transcript are digests: counts not lists, capped lists with an honest +N more
statement: State reported back into an agent's context window must be trimmed at the reporting seam: aggregate lists to counts where names add nothing ('the digest reports "2 live sessions", never names'), and cap enumerations at a small N with an explicit '…+N more' tail — ten plus an honest remainder tells the model the same thing a whole portfolio dump would, at a fraction of the tokens. Do the trimming in the bridge that formats the report, not in the underlying data model.

title: Give unattended automation three fire modes: auto, dry-run-suppress-outbound, and hold-for-approval
statement: Triggers that fire without a human present need a per-trigger unattended mode: 'auto' (fire normally), 'dry_run' (run the pipeline but suppress outbound side effects), and 'approval' (hold the fire in a pending queue until a human approves — approval publishes the held event and the run proceeds; rejection discards). The queue is first-class API surface (list pending fires, resolve by id) so any surface can build a review inbox over it.

title: Craft copilot prompts from the classifier's verdict: hand the agent a diagnosis to confirm, not a mystery to re-investigate
statement: When a UI asks an LLM copilot to reason about a stuck work unit, the prompt should be generated from the same typed state model the UI renders, live in one exported function next to that model (one source of truth for the wording), and branch on the diagnosis: a unit the classifier already knows is unrecoverable gets a prompt that states the diagnosis, forbids the futile action, and asks for a one-line confirmation — not an open-ended 'assess and unblock' that burns a full investigation to reach a conclusion the caller already had.

title: Enforce advisory LLM protocol rules with a host-side state machine that suppresses and synthesizes
statement: When a prompt rule says the model MUST ask before resolving a field, treat the rule as advisory: mirror it in a host-side per-entity gate state machine (Closed → Pending → Open) that suppresses out-of-order resolution events and locally synthesizes the clarifying question the model skipped. The model stays the primary author when it cooperates; synthesis is the fallback, so the UX never depends on model obedience.

title: Every ask-the-user guard needs a headless bypass, or autonomous runs loop forever
statement: Guards that exist to force a human question (gate suppression, ambiguity force-close, blocking on an answer channel) must be explicitly disabled or rerouted in headless/autonomous mode. Otherwise the guard re-fires every turn with nobody to answer, and the run spins until the turn budget or a timeout dies for it.

title: Early-stream only data the state machine doesn't own; keep the post-turn parse authoritative
statement: To cut perceived latency on a long LLM turn, accumulate partial-message deltas and emit a sub-object the moment its braces balance — but only for identity/display data that no downstream state machine consumes. The authoritative post-turn parse stays unchanged and dedup drops the duplicate, so the optimization is purely additive and can never corrupt gating logic.

title: Batch synthesized fallback questions per turn, and fan the answer across every pending gate
statement: A fallback that asks one question per model round-trip serializes the interview into minutes of dead time. Emit every still-closed gate's question in one batch (marking each Pending so it can't double-fire), and on answer receipt sweep ALL pending gates whose field matches an answered key — a singleton pending-slot handler will re-ask the questions the batch already covered.

title: Run intent heuristics on the user's raw words, never on the assembled prompt
statement: Keyword heuristics that scan 'the input' must scan the user's raw text. The assembled system prompt mentions every keyword the heuristic matches for (it documents the rules), so scanning it auto-triggers every branch. Thread the raw intent as its own parameter even when the full prompt is already in hand.

title: Auto-resolve only when EVERY matched binding is unambiguous — never early-return on the first clean match
statement: A matcher that returns 'auto-resolve' on the first unambiguous hit silently skips the later matches that needed disambiguation. Scan all matches first: any ambiguous hit (e.g. a service with 2+ vault credentials) forces the question; only when every matched service is unambiguous may the gate auto-open — and log which services forced it.

title: Give each parallel sub-agent its siblings' scope as an explicit not-your-job list
statement: When fanning one model conversation out into per-unit sub-agents, each sub-prompt must carry (a) the fixed shared identity, (b) the single unit to resolve, (c) the sibling units labeled explicitly as owned-by-others so the agent doesn't re-implement them, and (d) a hard rule to never bind an unconfirmed provider/destination — bind only from the supplied list, preferring fewer bindings when in doubt.

title: A one-shot correction is a --print call, not a re-entry into the multi-turn runner
statement: When an autonomous flow needs a single LLM edit (fix a broken artifact given a failure summary), spawn a one-shot print invocation rather than reusing the multi-turn streaming runner. Document the why-not-reuse at the module head: the runner's event protocol and gate scaffolding would all need carving out, and the fix is advisory — the caller decides whether to commit it.

title: Gate a session-open LLM briefing on a computed delta — quiet means no model call
statement: Before firing an LLM to compose a 'while you were away' briefing, build a serializable delta document from data already on hand and run a triviality gate over it. A trivial delta renders an honest deterministic 'quiet night' state with zero model calls and no navigation hijack; only a real delta spends the LLM, and even then a deterministic fallback composition (same widget vocabulary) covers null/failed responses so the surface never degrades to an error.

title: Verify model output against a server-built fact digest
statement: Telling a model to use only the figures you supplied reduces fabrication but does not prevent it. Build the fact digest server-side from deterministic tools, then check the reply afterwards: any number absent from the digest means the whole answer is discarded and the deterministic fallback ships instead. The prompt asks; the post-hoc check enforces.

title: Repair model JSON syntactically and boundedly, never semantically
statement: Models drop trailing braces on long output and wrap objects in prose, and both are recoverable without guessing. Append only the missing closing braces, only when the text does not end inside a string literal and the deficit is small, keeping the original parse error otherwise — and locate an envelope by scanning for its key and brace-matching with string awareness, from exactly one shared function, because copies of that loop drift into panics.

title: Frame pasted user material as reference, never as instructions
statement: When grounding a generation in user-supplied context (writing samples, role docs, brand guides), the prompt must explicitly frame the block as reference material — mirror its tone, take its facts — while forbidding obedience to any instructions embedded inside it, and bound it with a char-safe truncation that appends a visible truncation note.

title: Pair every prompt-level rule with a backend fallback for that failure
statement: A rule added to a prompt lowers the probability of a failure; it does not remove it. For any failure whose signature is a silent no-op, ship the prompt change together with a backend counterpart — a fallback that recovers, or a rejection that is fed back — and decide deliberately which half of each constraint is machine-enforced, since a prompt-level cap only makes the model stop reading early.

title: Keep the dispatch prompt beside its deserializer, ship vocab as data
statement: For a prompt that drives a machine-readable result, three things belong together and nowhere else: the prompt string, the output contract and the dedup key, with the deserializer named as the other half of one contract. Any closed vocabulary both sides must agree on lives in exactly one place and travels to the agent as data in its input file — restating it in prose is how parallel agents fragment it.

title: Let an agent refuse, and make it confess what it did not cover
statement: An automated agent that cannot say 'this does not apply' will always find a way to apply it, producing cargo-culted changes that look like output. Write the refusal into the instruction as a valid outcome with its own verdict token so it is machine-countable, and require a statement of what was not covered — honest thin results beat padded ones, but only the confession makes the difference visible.

title: Mine your corpus for the option set and ship each option's directive
statement: Behaviour dials invented by a designer rarely match how the artifacts actually vary. Derive the option vocabulary from the corpus you already have, and store the exact prompt sentence on the same record as the label and the icon, so a user's selection compiles into a directive block mechanically and an untouched picker contributes nothing to the prompt.

title: Strip forged delimiters from untrusted text in one shared helper
statement: Third-party text fenced into a prompt can close its own fence and continue as instructions. Sanitize every untrusted blob through one provider-neutral helper that removes any copy of the chosen delimiter before embedding, keep it shared by every prompt path so a hardening change cannot land on one path and not the other, and record the residual gaps honestly instead of implying the problem is closed.

title: Assume user text will forge your line format — escape or sentinel it
statement: Any line-oriented structure you compose into a prompt or an agent payload is forgeable by the text you interpolate into it. Either escape the delimiter on the way in, or mark machine-emitted headers with a character the user cannot type, and keep that logic in one helper every call path uses — divergence between two call paths is exactly how the security-relevant half gets skipped.

title: Defend prompts structurally: sanitize, nonce boundaries, canary
statement: A blocklist of injection phrases fails on the first rephrasing. Defend on structure instead: truncate, strip invisible and non-BMP characters, remove role lines and section delimiters, neutralise recursive template syntax, then wrap the value in a boundary tag carrying a per-execution nonce so injected content cannot close it, and instruct the model to report manipulation attempts. Keep the module private to prompt assembly so no other code can bypass it.

title: Leave unresolved placeholders visible so bad output is greppable
statement: A substitution engine that silently emits empty strings hides its own failures inside plausible-looking output. Distinguish three cases and encode intent in each: an unknown variable keeps its placeholder so the output stays searchable, an intentionally skipped optional binding becomes empty, and a required binding with no value stays visible — paired with a validator that catches required gaps before substitution runs, not after.

title: Version the system prompt like code, one changelog entry per fix
statement: Treat the system prompt as a versioned artifact: bump a number on every behaviour-affecting change, record the observed failure and the specific edit next to it, and persist the version with each session so cross-version behaviour is auditable. Validate with a multi-run sweep, since one failed run is variance while the same failure across four is a systematic gap — and remember placement matters as much as wording.

title: Treat LLM stream-json assistant events as cumulative and emit only the computed delta
statement: Claude CLI stream-json assistant events re-send the whole turn's text every time; forwarding them naively duplicates every line downstream. Keep a per-turn accumulator, emit new[acc.len()..] when the new text is a superset, skip subsets, and reset the accumulator when a tool result signals a new turn.

title: Failover chains that pin model ids rot into guaranteed failure
statement: A model-fallback ladder hardcoding provider model ids will eventually hand a healthy run to a retired id — turning failover into a guaranteed 404. Keep the chain on the same canonical current ids the rest of the codebase bakes into configs, and pin it with a regression test asserting retired ids are unreachable.

title: Give a scan a third verdict for 'does not apply here'
statement: Holds/doesn't-hold is a false dichotomy for a portfolio: add `applies: bool` (default true) so practices from another stack aren't filed as work owed (7 Next.js practices had been filed as owed by a Tauri app).

title: Resolve model-named entities against the real map; drop what doesn't resolve
statement: Resolve every entity the model names against the real map; drop what doesn't resolve, refuse the result if nothing does, and let a primary outside the slice fall back to one inside it.

title: When filtering an LLM-returned array, REMAP the indices its cross-references use
statement: members[] + connections[] are keyed by 0-based indices; build an old_idx→new_idx map, drop edges referencing removed members plus self-loops — skipping the remap silently rewires the graph.

title: Make automated bypasses of a human queue visible, detected from the writer's stable markers
statement: When a policy (trust_llm / auto-triage) resolves items without a human and there is no structured column recording that, detect it from the exact machine markers the backend writes into the notes field, render a visible badge with the machine's reasoning, and pin the producer's exact strings in tests naming the Rust source sites.

title: Parse LLM-emitted UI specs forgiving-in bounded-out, with a per-item salvage pass that reports drops
statement: Schema-validate agent-emitted structures with coercing, clamping, truncating field types (percent clamps rather than rejects; text coerces primitives and truncates); strict-parse the whole document first, and on failure salvage every individually valid block, surface the dropped count to the user rather than hiding it, and fail only when NOTHING renderable survives — at which point fall back to plain markdown.

title: Zero can mean unknown: exclude cost-unknown candidates from value rankings instead of treating 0 as free
statement: A provider whose per-call cost is hardcoded 0.0 (because it is UNKNOWN, e.g. local models) scores as a perfect-efficiency free model in any cost-weighted value ranking and always wins. Model 'cost unknown' as an explicit flag and exclude flagged candidates from best-value verdicts entirely — returning 'unknown' when every candidate is flagged — rather than letting a sentinel zero masquerade as free.

title: A model's self-asserted success flag is not evidence — count it UNVERIFIED and hold promotion without burning retries
statement: In a pre-promote test gate over model-produced reports, distinguish four verdicts: pass (a call was actually made, or a code-authored allowlist vouches for a built-in), skipped, failed, and UNVERIFIED (the model claimed success without a verifiable call). Unverified is a third outcome distinct from pass and fail: it holds promotion but is not fed to the fix-retry loop, because there is nothing for a correction pass to 'fix'. A malformed/unreadable report is likewise Held with a per-field reason, never Pass.

title: Merge batch LLM verdicts fail-closed: omitted rejects, inexact token rejects, unknown id drops, duplicate ignored
statement: Three independent batch-decision modules converge on one merge discipline: an id the model never returned is rejected (a dropped line must never read as approval), a verdict token that is not exactly the accept literal degrades to reject, hallucinated ids are dropped so they cannot create phantom rows, and duplicate verdicts for one item are ignored after the first (which also prevents a count underflow). An empty sanitized result is an Err so the caller falls back to deterministic composition instead of rendering a stub.

title: Put the safety floor in code and tell the model the override exists
statement: High-priority items are forced to the safe action in code regardless of the model's verdict, unknown verdict tokens also land on the safe action, and the prompt states that the override exists so the model is not fighting a hidden rule. Every auto-resolve is annotated with an audit note so the decision is explainable after the fact.

title: Require provenance at the writer, and validate every model-supplied id against live rows AND the ids that were in the prompt
statement: Derived-memory writes are rejected without at least one source episode id, so the model cannot bury an invention by leaving the field empty. Any id the model hands back (supersedes, winner/loser, provenance) is checked against live DB rows and against the exact id set that was in the prompt — a hallucinated id drops the candidate rather than demoting an arbitrary record.

title: Parse structured trailing markers out of LLM prose — strip the marker line even when it does not parse
statement: For sidechannel-in-prose protocols (a trailing MARKER: {json} line), the extractor must strip the marker line unconditionally so a malformed marker never leaks to the user, take only the first occurrence, accept a structured envelope OR a plain-text fallback, keep enum-ish fields as strings so a hallucinated value degrades one field instead of voiding the parse, and whitelist constrained fields on extraction.

title: When an LLM refines an authored artifact, merge back only the prose and reject collapsed outputs — the result must never be worse than the base
statement: An LLM 'specialization' pass over an authored artifact needs three structural guarantees: (1) only the prose fields (system prompt, instructions) are merged back — the deterministic structure (use cases, triggers, connectors) is never touched by the model; (2) every failure path (spawn error, unparseable output, nothing to merge) keeps the base and returns adjusted:false with a note, so the flow is never worse than the deterministic path; (3) a quality gate rejects a non-empty output whose prose collapsed to a fraction of the authored base (e.g. < 40% of a base > 200 chars) — truncation and models that gut the prompt are real, and 'shorter' must not silently replace 'authored'. Scale the model to divergence: defaults get a cheap wire-only pass, configured adoptions get a fuller model, escalated when the artifact carries high-stakes capabilities.

title: Verify a freshly minted artifact with a real run and map the outcome three ways: proven, hard-block, or visibly unverified
statement: After generating/adopting an artifact that claims to work (an agent, a pipeline, an integration), run one real verification of its first capability and refuse the binary pass/fail frame. Three-way mapping: value delivered → verified, status untouched; hard failure (precondition/failed) → downgrade the artifact's status so the run path blocks until fixed, AND raise a review; soft outcomes (no input available, unassessable, event-only) → leave it runnable but raise a visible review stating it was minted unverified. The one forbidden outcome is the old behaviour: silently presenting an unproven artifact as ready. Skip the run entirely when the artifact is already flagged (redundant cost), and make the gate fail-open — a verification that cannot be assessed must not brick a working artifact.

title: An optional prop that is the sole conduit of a feedback loop can silently sever it — wire it at every call site and say it is load-bearing
statement: When human feedback flows to a learning/improvement engine only through one UI prop, shipping a call site without that prop closes the entire loop with zero errors: the feature keeps rendering, the table that feeds the improver just never gets rows. Audit that every renderer of the feedback control passes the persistence props, and leave a comment at the call site naming the downstream consumer so the next refactor cannot drop it unknowingly.

title: A relevance threshold calibrated on identical-text fixtures never fires on real inputs
statement: Avoid tuning a match/suggestion threshold against verbatim-copy fixtures: real paraphrased inputs score far below identical text under weighted overlap, so the feature silently never triggers. Calibrate against the realistic score band and write the band math into the constant's comment.

title: Apply selecting filters before the top-k cut; only thresholds may come after
statement: Truncating a ranked candidate pool to top_k before a selecting filter (scope/path) returns 'whichever of the global top-k happen to match' — often zero. Carry the bounded pool through filtering and cut afterwards; pure thresholds like min_score remain correct post-cut. Pin both directions with regression tests.

title: Keyword matching over non-English input needs an ASCII service-name substring scan
statement: Word-splitting keyword extraction fails on CJK (no spaces) and joined scripts — but product/service names ('gmail', 'notion', 'slack') are written in ASCII in every locale. Supplement tokenization with a substring scan for the canonical service-name list (sourced from the live registry plus a fallback), so matching works for all languages; find 'gmail' inside 'Gmailのメール'.

title: Budget recall per lane with floors; compress above a threshold only
statement: Injecting whatever the vector search returned produces incoherent context. Split recall into named lanes with a documented cap each, and give the lanes that carry identity — facts, active goals, standing rules, open commitments — an unconditional floor so an off-topic query cannot evict them. Over-fetch once and split by kind in application code when the search itself is the expensive step, and add a compression pass only above a token threshold, failing through to raw chunks.

title: Stamp each vector with its embedding model and filter recall on it
statement: Vectors written under different embedding models share a table but not a space, so querying across them returns confidently wrong neighbours with no error raised anywhere. Store the model and dimensions on each row, filter recall to the currently loaded model, count and log the exclusions instead of dropping them silently, and grandfather rows written before stamping existed so the guard is a no-op until a model actually changes.

title: Fuse heterogeneous retrievers by rank, not by normalized score
statement: Lexical, semantic and graph retrievers produce scores on incomparable scales, so any cross-retriever normalization is a guess dressed as arithmetic. Fuse on rank instead, with an optional weight toward the lexical list for identifier-heavy queries, and keep tie-breaks deterministic so the same inputs always yield the same ordering.
